title: Understand Shielded Bitcoin from end to end
mission: Explain the full system accurately in a presentation and handle questions about its mechanisms, privacy, assumptions, and open research
next_action: All core modules and both optional extensions are available. Start with M01 for the full sequence or resume F01 for the requested proof foundations; adapt review from learner responses
progress_policy: Generated material is not completed learning. Update learning_status only from learner evidence, link that evidence in learning-records, and select the next lesson from prerequisites and demonstrated gaps
session_pattern: Recall one prior idea without hints; take one short HTML lesson; try a new case with immediate feedback; explain the result; revisit it in a later session

cook.title: Cook: The P versus NP Problem

groth.title: Groth: On the Size of Pairing-based Non-interactive Arguments

phases.title: Foundations and the problem
phases.outcome: Explain Bitcoin’s public ledger, the proof vocabulary, and who checks each part of Shielded Bitcoin
phases.checkpoint: Explain a statement, witness, proof and zk-SNARK in plain English, then assign publication, transfer checks and key release to the correct components

modules.title: Bitcoin’s public ledger
modules.topics: UTXOs, transaction inputs and outputs, change, signatures, fees, confirmation, and observable payment relationships
modules.win: Read a small Bitcoin transaction and separate public facts from ownership guesses
modules.exercise: Label the public amounts and links in a payment with change, then identify which ownership claims require extra evidence

modules.title: The cryptographic vocabulary
modules.topics: Hashing, commitments, encryption and signatures; a first distinction between hiding data and proving a claim
modules.win: Choose the right primitive for hiding data, committing to data, authorizing a spend, or proving a condition
modules.exercise: Assign a primitive to four protocol tasks and explain what each one does not establish

modules.title: Statements, witnesses and checking rules
modules.topics: Public inputs, claims, witnesses, relations, and the separate proof object
modules.win: Describe a claim and its evidence before using cryptographic notation
modules.exercise: Construct and check a subset totaling 31, then distinguish a private transfer witness from its public proof

modules.title: P, NP and the open question
modules.topics: Decision problems, polynomial time, efficient witness checks, P contained in NP, and what remains unproved
modules.win: Explain NP without claiming it means hard or non-polynomial
modules.exercise: Compare combinations with checking one witness, and explain why brute-force growth is not a lower bound

modules.title: What zero knowledge adds
modules.topics: Prover, verifier, completeness, soundness, privacy relative to public inputs, and encryption versus proof
modules.win: Explain how proof validity and witness privacy are separate properties
modules.exercise: Compare sending private evidence, merely asserting validity, and sending a zero-knowledge proof

modules.title: SNARKs, circuits and constraints
modules.topics: Succinctness, non-interactivity, arguments, knowledge, zk-SNARKs, constraints, Groth16 and trusted setup
modules.win: Expand SNARK accurately and explain how payment rules become proof constraints
modules.exercise: Check balanced amounts with negative change to discover why balance needs range checks

modules.title: The complete system map
modules.topics: Wallets, Bitcoin publication and ordering, replaying indexers, shielded state, and entry/exit boundaries
modules.win: Place each responsibility with the component that performs it
modules.exercise: Sort actions among wallet, Bitcoin, indexer and an unspecified peg component

phases.title: Build a private spend
phases.outcome: Explain how ownership stays private while invalid spending is rejected
phases.checkpoint: Explain why ciphertext, a membership proof, and a nullifier are each necessary, then predict a repeated-spend attempt and a forged-nullifier attempt

modules.title: Notes, addresses and encrypted outputs
modules.topics: The (v, d, rseed) plaintext, recipient addresses, derived per-note values, ciphertexts and public leaves
modules.win: Separate a private note from its encrypted representation and its tree leaf
modules.exercise: Sort one output’s fields into private, encrypted and public, then identify what a recipient recovers

modules.title: Merkle membership and one global tree
modules.topics: Leaves, positions, hashes, Merkle paths, roots, and append-only growth
modules.win: Explain what a root and membership path establish without treating membership as proof of an unspent note
modules.exercise: Append two outputs to a small tree and trace which hashes and paths change

modules.title: Nullifiers and double-spend prevention
modules.topics: Nullifier secret, note randomness, canonical position, deterministic derivation and the accepted nullifier set
modules.win: Explain why a new transaction or new anchor cannot give the same note a fresh valid spend marker
modules.exercise: Predict replay outcomes for a first spend, a repeated marker, and a forged fresh marker

modules.title: What the transfer proof actually proves
modules.topics: Public inputs, private witness, membership, spend authority, nullifier derivation, output encryption, amount ranges, exact conservation and body binding
modules.win: State the proof’s job and distinguish it from checks performed by replay
modules.exercise: Break a transfer in several ways and identify the failed constraint or replay rule

phases.title: Publish, replay and settle
phases.outcome: Follow an entire transfer and reconstruct its effect on shared state
phases.checkpoint: Replay a short block sequence with accepted and rejected transfers, keep both indexers consistent, and explain what a reorganization changes

modules.title: Alice pays Bob, end to end
modules.topics: Synchronize, select notes and anchor, create payment and change, encrypt, prove, publish, replay, detect receipt
modules.win: Narrate a payment without confusing wallet intent, Bitcoin confirmation and shielded acceptance
modules.exercise: Put shuffled transfer events in order and identify when Bob has an accepted note

modules.title: Envelope, carrier and body binding
modules.topics: Canonical encoding, h_body, proof binding, OP_RETURN and witness carriers, policy versus consensus, external Bitcoin fees
modules.win: Distinguish the transfer body, proof and carrier transaction, including who pays the fee
modules.exercise: Tamper with a body-bound field and explain why the old proof cannot validate the changed envelope

modules.title: Deterministic replay and indexer trust
modules.topics: Parsing, body binding, anchor checks, nullifier checks, proof verification, atomic updates, note tree, nullifier set, root history and accepted history
modules.win: Explain why indexers independently reconstruct copies of one logical state and how an unverified response can mislead a wallet
modules.exercise: Run two indexers over the same blocks, reject an invalid envelope, and compare their resulting state

modules.title: Anchors, confirmations and reorganizations
modules.topics: Per-block roots, the valid-root window, minimum depth, wallet confirmation policy, expiration and chain replacement
modules.win: Explain why a stale proof may need rebuilding while the underlying note remains recoverable
modules.exercise: Classify valid, too-new and expired anchors, then rebuild a transfer after its anchor block is replaced

phases.title: Wallets, recovery and privacy
phases.outcome: Explain what users can spend, recover, reveal and still leak
phases.checkpoint: Explain recovery after losing a wallet, predict the effects of sharing each capability, and assess a transfer from an observer’s perspective

modules.title: Keys and separate capabilities
modules.topics: Seed, master key, spending secret, nullifier secret, incoming viewing, outgoing recovery and diversified addresses
modules.win: Distinguish spending authority from detection, viewing and nullifier-linking capabilities
modules.exercise: Build a capability map and explain the consequences of leaking each key

modules.title: Recovery from seed and history
modules.topics: Incoming scanning, outgoing recovery, positions, spent status, trusted indexer reliance and bootstrap recovery data
modules.win: Describe the data and checks needed to reconstruct spendable wallet state
modules.exercise: Recover a small wallet ledger from accepted envelopes and identify what seed-only restoration still depends on

modules.title: Privacy guarantees and metadata
modules.topics: Observer models, amounts and relationships, anonymity sets, timing, arity, anchor age, shared output grouping, fee funding, boundary events and network-scope limits
modules.win: Explain why cryptographic hiding does not guarantee an observer cannot infer a payment
modules.exercise: Evaluate several transfers with different metadata and justify which candidate inputs can actually be excluded

modules.title: Disclosure and audit claims
modules.topics: IncomingView, OutgoingView, NoteOpening, DerivedReport, policy scope versus cryptographic scope, and read-only access
modules.win: Choose the least revealing evidence for a concrete audit question
modules.exercise: Match three audit requests to disclosure methods and explain what each does and does not prove

phases.title: Covenants, witness encryption and PIPEs
phases.outcome: Connect the transfer protocol to proposed Bitcoin spending control without overclaiming the peg
phases.checkpoint: Explain the three different proof roles, what PIPEs releases, what it does not constrain afterward, and which object has the large size estimate

modules.title: Covenants and transaction restrictions
modules.topics: Authorization, output restrictions, transaction templates and conditional key release
modules.win: Distinguish permission to sign from restrictions on the transaction being signed
modules.exercise: Compare a template-constrained spend with a condition that merely releases an ordinary signing key

modules.title: Witness encryption from first principles
modules.topics: Statements, relations, witnesses, message encryption and recovery, a SNARK proof as a witness, and extractable security
modules.win: Explain how a condition can control decryption without confusing WE with ordinary note encryption
modules.exercise: Construct a simple statement/witness pair, then replace the witness with proof-verification evidence

modules.title: PIPEs v2 and the unfinished peg boundary
modules.topics: Encrypting a Schnorr key, setup consistency proofs, proposed MPC setup, witness-gated recovery, ordinary Bitcoin signing, and peg-in/peg-out scope
modules.win: Describe the PIPE mechanism while separating transfer validity, key release and a complete BTC entry/exit design
modules.exercise: Draw the proof-to-key-to-signature path and list the additional questions a complete peg specification must answer

modules.title: Why the WE ciphertext is so large
modules.topics: AADP verifier encoding, variables and constraints, matrix size, succinct witnesses, verifier optimization and modeled costs
modules.win: Distinguish proof size, envelope size and WE ciphertext size, and explain what different forms of compression would target
modules.exercise: Vary the verifier cost model and explain why reducing two counts has an approximately cubic size effect

phases.title: Evaluate and present the whole proposal
phases.outcome: Give an accurate explanation and handle questions you have not rehearsed
phases.checkpoint: Deliver a short presentation, answer new failure scenarios, and clearly label specified behavior, assumptions, estimates and open work

modules.title: Security assumptions and failure modes
modules.topics: Proof soundness and zero knowledge, trusted setup, hash binding, encryption, wallet compromise, data availability, malicious indexers and WE heuristic security
modules.win: Connect a failed assumption to the particular guarantee it threatens
modules.exercise: Evaluate a compromised setup, a lying indexer, a leaked viewing key and a stolen spending key without treating them as equivalent

modules.title: Tradeoffs, alternatives and deployment gaps
modules.topics: CoinJoin, PayJoin, Silent Payments, Zcash, Monero and Shielded CSV comparisons; arity, proof/carrier costs, policy dependencies, light clients, private fees, and incomplete deployment choices
modules.win: Compare designs by validation, data availability, leakage and assumptions rather than by slogans
modules.exercise: Fill a comparison matrix, reconcile envelope versus carrier cost, and classify proposal claims by evidential status

modules.title: Presentation and audience questions
modules.topics: A coherent explanation, concrete failure scenarios, source-backed answers, and handling unspecified details
modules.win: Explain the full system in ten minutes and answer five unfamiliar questions without overclaiming
modules.exercise: Rehearse from a blank system map; explain one payment; then answer questions about duplicate spends, malicious indexers, reorgs, setup, recovery, fees and entry/exit

optional_extensions.goal: Trace private witness values through the constraint blocks and identify which profile choices are required for interoperable implementations
